```{r}
source(here::here("R/load.R"))

```

This project collects data about Framingham, Massachusetts and puts it in a form that's easy to analyze. It focuses on **election results** -- City and Town races, state and federal races in Framingham, and turnout, all by precinct -- and also has precinct and district maps, property records and Census data.

Every dataset is here in two forms: the **original files** (the clerk's PDFs, downloaded shapefiles, and so on, in `data-raw/`) and **analysis-friendly versions** (in `data/`).

## Quick start

All election results are in one file, one row per election, race, candidate and precinct. In R:

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
library(dplyr)
results <- readr::read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smach/Framingham-City-Data/main/data/elections/results_precinct.csv")

# Every mayoral race, candidates only (no blanks or write-ins)
results |>
  filter(office == "Mayor", candidate_type == "candidate") |>
  group_by(election_date, type, candidate) |>
  summarize(votes = sum(votes), .groups = "drop")
```

The same files open in Excel, Python, Datawrapper or anything else that reads CSV.

## The main files

```{r}
main <- data.frame(
  File = c("data/elections/results_precinct.csv", "data/elections/results_district.csv",
           "data/elections/turnout_precinct.csv", "data/elections/turnout_district.csv",
           "data/elections/turnout_citywide.csv", "data/elections/elections.csv",
           "data/elections/by_election/", "data/gis/framingham_precincts.gpkg"),
  What = c("All results by precinct (tidy format)", "All results by city council district",
           "Turnout by precinct", "Turnout by city council district", "Citywide turnout, one row per election",
           "List of elections, including ones not yet collected",
           "One file per election, laid out like the clerk's table (easy to read in Excel)",
           "Precinct boundaries for both precinct maps, with city council districts")
)
main$File <- vapply(main$File, link, character(1))
knitr::kable(main, escape = FALSE)
```

### What the columns mean

**results_precinct.csv**

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| election_id | Unique ID: date, level and type, e.g. `2023-11-07_municipal_general` |
| election_date | Date of the election |
| level | `municipal` (City/Town) or `state` (state and federal offices, primaries) |
| type | `general`, `preliminary`, `special`, `town` (pre-2018 annual town election), `primary`, `presidential-primary` |
| status | `official` or `unofficial` (election-night) results |
| party | For primaries, the party ballot; otherwise empty |
| race | The race exactly as the clerk printed it |
| office | Standardized office name, e.g. `City Council At-Large`, `School Committee District`, `State Representative` |
| office_district | District number or name for district offices, e.g. `3` or `6th Middlesex` |
| seats | Number of seats being elected, when printed |
| candidate | Candidate name as printed; `Blanks` and `Write-ins` are standardized |
| candidate_type | `candidate`, `blank`, `write-in`, or `response` (Yes/No on ballot questions) |
| precinct | Precinct as printed, including sub-precincts such as `9A` |
| precinct_base | Precinct without the sub-precinct letter (`9A` -> `9`) |
| city_district | City council district the precinct was in **on that date** (empty before 2012) |
| votes | Votes |

**turnout_precinct.csv** has the same election columns plus `registered`, `ballots_cast` and `turnout_pct` (always a percent from 0 to 100). For primaries there's a row per party ballot as well as an all-voters row (empty `party`).

**About precincts:** Framingham's precincts were redrawn after the 2020 Census. The 18-precinct map was used through the January 11 2022 special election; the 27-precinct map since the September 2022 state primary. Precinct "4" is a different place on each map, so always look at `election_date` (or use `city_district`, which is correct for each date).

## Citywide turnout

```{r}
t <- turnout[is.na(turnout$party), c("election_date", "election_id", "registered", "ballots_cast", "turnout_pct")]
t$election <- elections$name[match(t$election_id, elections$election_id)]
t <- t[order(t$election_date, decreasing = TRUE), c("election_date", "election", "registered", "ballots_cast", "turnout_pct")]
names(t) <- c("Date", "Election", "Registered", "Ballots cast", "Turnout %")
knitr::kable(t, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

## Elections

Elections marked "No" haven't been collected yet. If you have the clerk's results for one, see *How the data are maintained* below.

```{r}
e <- elections[order(elections$election_date, decreasing = TRUE), c("election_date", "name", "status", "has_data", "notes")]
e$has_data <- ifelse(e$has_data, "Yes", "No")
e$status[is.na(e$status)] <- ""
e$notes[is.na(e$notes)] <- ""
names(e) <- c("Date", "Election", "Status", "Have data?", "Notes")
DT::datatable(e, rownames = FALSE, options = list(pageLength = 10))
```

## Search all files

Every file in the project. The search boxes accept regular expressions.

```{r}
catalog <- build_file_catalog()
catalog$File <- vapply(catalog$File, link, character(1))
DT::datatable(catalog, filter = "top", rownames = FALSE, escape = FALSE,
              options = list(pageLength = 15, lengthMenu = c(10, 15, 25, 50, 100), search = list(regex = TRUE)))
```

## Maps

The precinct files in `data/gis/` work in any mapping tool. In R, `make_precinct_map()` in `r link("R/gis.R")` makes an interactive map of precincts colored by city council district and searchable by address:

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
source("R/load.R")
make_precinct_map("2023-11-07", show_house_districts = TRUE)
```

## How the data are maintained

* **Sources.** Local election results come from the Framingham City Clerk's results PDFs. They're turned into spreadsheets (with CometDocs or PDFTables for older elections, Adobe Acrobat from 2024 on), and every election is **checked automatically**: each row's precinct numbers must add up to the clerk's total, ballots can't exceed registered voters, and so on. The checks for every election are in `r link("data/elections/validation_report.csv")`.
* **Automation.** A scheduled GitHub Action looks for new results on the clerk's page. When it finds some, it extracts and checks them and opens a pull request for a human to review before anything is published.
* **Reproducible.** Everything in `data/elections/` is rebuilt from `data-raw/` by `r link("scripts/build_all.R")`; nothing there is edited by hand. The R code is in `r link("R/")`, and the README explains how to add an election.

_This is an unofficial project and isn't affiliated with the City of Framingham. Check official sources before relying on the data for anything important._
